messages:
alex: Hey team — after switching the JS SDK to ESM and publishing, our sample app on the Vercel Edge runtime started blowing up in prod with a weird runtime error: `TypeError: createClient is not a function`. Works fine in Node & in local dev builds though.

alex: Quick stack: `at /_edge_handler (index.js:54:12)` — the error points at the line where we `import { createClient } from 'redwood-sdk'` and call it.

alex: Repro steps I used: `git clone git+https://git.company/sample-app`, `cd sample-app`, `npm i`, `npm run build && vercel --prod` — edge deploy. Fails on cold start.

maya: ugh. did you check the published package files? sometimes bundlers/rollups tree-shake the side-effectful registration (polyfills or runtime glue) if package.json has "sideEffects": false.

alex: omg yes — our SDK has "sideEffects": false in package.json because we wanted maximal tree-shaking. But we also have a small file `src/register-globals.ts` that mutates globalThis for edge (adds fetch polyfill & attaches helpers). I think it got removed.

alex: in the built ESM bundle `dist/index.esm.js` I don't see the register import anywhere. In the CJS build it was imported in the entry and worked.

tj: two separate problems colliding: (1) ESM vs CJS export shape (default vs named) and (2) sideEffects tree-shaking removing a module that does necessary global mutation. Edge bundlers are aggressive.

tj: quick checks: 1) open the published tarball (npm pack) and `tar -tf <pkg.tgz>` to verify dist files. 2) inspect package.json fields: `main`, `module`, `exports`, `type`. If `module` points to ESM but `exports` maps don't include the side-effect entry, it can be omitted by bundlers.

maya: do you have an `index.js` that just re-exports from `./dist`? we sometimes accidentally ship an index that *only* has `export { default } from './lib'` which doesn't import side-effect file. If sideEffects=false and register file is imported only for side effects, bundlers will remove it.

alex: here's our package.json excerpt from the published package:```json
{
  "name": "redwood-sdk",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "type": "module",
  "main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
  "module": "dist/index.esm.js",
  "sideEffects": false,
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "dist/index.esm.js",
      "require": "dist/index.cjs.js"
    }
  }
}
```

alex: and our dist entry `dist/index.esm.js` is a tiny re-export file: `export * from './runtime.js'; export { default } from './runtime.js';` — runtime.js internally imports `./register-globals.js` but because register is only imported conditionally in build-time it got tree-shaken.

tj: immediate mitigation: mark the register file as side-effectful so bundlers keep it. e.g. set `"sideEffects": ["./dist/register-globals.js"]` (or better: adjust build to import it from the entry so it's visible). That should restore behaviour for edge runtimes.

maya: also consider using the `exports` map to expose a side-effect entry explicitly: `"./edge": { "import": "dist/edge-init.js" }` and ask consumers to import `'redwood-sdk/edge'` in edge-only entrypoints. Dirty but explicit.

alex: I tried updating package.json to `"sideEffects": ["dist/register-globals.js"]` and republished. Edge deploy stopped throwing the createClient error — yay. But bundle size increased ~120KB (gzip) because the register file pulls in a big debug util that we thought tree-shaking would remove.

tj: yeah that's the tradeoff. Marking file as side-effectful prevents tree-shaking within it for top-level imports. Two fixes: (A) move minimal runtime mutations into a very small file with zero deps, keep heavy debug-only code behind a lazy `if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production')` or dynamic import, or (B) keep `sideEffects: false` but rework entry to explicitly import register so it won't be removed. The latter keeps tree-shaking granularity better.

maya: FYI for ESM/CJS parity: ensure you export named functions instead of relying on `module.exports = fn` / default interop. Many bundlers (and edge runtimes) choke on `interopDefault` wrappers when tree-shaken. Use rollup/esbuild produced ESM with named exports and a CJS build for Node consumers. The `exports` map can point to both correctly.

alex: for us the bigger DX problem is sample app onboarding: the quickstart imports `import { createClient } from 'redwood-sdk'` in a file that runs on the edge. If consumers blindly copy/paste, they hit this. We should add a note in the README and example: `// for Edge runtimes import 'redwood-sdk/register-edge'` or update template to import side-effect entry.

tj: agree. Also add a smoke test in CI that builds the sample app with `vercel build` / `wrangler` for each publish to catch regressions. I can add a GH action that runs a minimal edge build.

ci-bot: ran quick smoke build on tag v1.2.1 — build failed earlier, now passes on `edge-init` branch. link: https://ci.company/builds/1482

maya: follow-up tasks: - Make `register-globals` tiny + lazy-load debug util - Add `redwood-sdk/edge` alias in exports - Update quickstart to import edge init - Add CI smoke test for edge build

alex: I'm going to roll a patch that: moves register into `src/edge/init.ts` (no deps), updates package.json `exports` with `./edge`, and keeps `sideEffects: false`. Then we can avoid bundle bloat and keep tree-shaking working.

alex: thanks for the help — putting notes in the sample-app README and a small CHANGELOG entry. If anyone wants to review the PR: https://github.com/company/redwood-sdk/pull/234

tj: LGTM once CI green. Also add unit test that asserts `node -e "import('redwood-sdk').then(m=>console.log(typeof m.createClient))"` returns 'function' in both node and a simulated bundler (esbuild build+run) if possible.

maya: nice. we should also add docs in the SDK DX page about `sideEffects` and how tree-shaking can remove runtime initializers — common pitfall for ESM-first packages. :warning:

alex: will do. :thumbsup:
